public_rationale: Ramp confirms concentrated spending in its sample. CNBC's August report establishes an enterprise majority at OpenAI, but gives no percentage establishing or excluding a vast majority. Neither source establishes the customer count or financing dependency. These gaps leave the compound claim unresolved; there is no sufficient basis for a mixed or contradicted verdict.
limitations: Several distinct financial propositions are bundled together.
The count and startup fraction are qualified rather than precisely asserted.
The unspecified accounting basis prevents a decisive comparison of the compound revenue claim.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: 80% of OpenAI and Anthropic's enterprise revenues, which make up the vast majority of their total revenues, depend on what are likely hundreds of customers spending outsized amounts on AI tokens, an indeterminately-large chunk of them AI startups that can only do so as long as venture capital supports them.
conditions: what are likely hundreds of customers

statement.excerpt: This means that 80% of OpenAI and Anthropic’s enterprise revenues — which make up the vast majority of their total revenues — are dependent on what are likely hundreds of customers spending outsized amounts of money on AI tokens, with an indeterminately-large chunk of them being AI startups that can only do so as long as venture capital supports them.

from_speaker: 80% of OpenAI and Anthropic’s enterprise revenues
the vast majority of their total revenues
AI startups that can only do so as long as venture capital supports them
our_interpretation: This is a compound claim about customer concentration, enterprise revenue share, approximate customer count, and financing dependency.
The ordinary reading of vast majority is clear dominance of enterprise revenue over other revenue, rather than merely crossing one half.
Read the enterprise-share assertion as applying to both named companies; the wording could alternatively refer to their combined revenue.
Treat hundreds as an approximate scale claim, not an exact count.
The startup fraction is explicitly unspecified, so no numerical threshold is invented.
Use August 2026, the last complete month before publication and the month of the located current revenue-mix disclosure.
Ramp provides an estimated concentration measure; the accounting basis for the broader revenue mix and dependency assertions is not supplied.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable evidence establishes the concentration figure, enterprise revenue clearly dominating total revenue at both labs, an approximately hundreds-sized customer group, and a material startup component unable to sustain payments without venture support.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence clearly refutes a firm component, such as showing that enterprise revenue does not dominate total revenue, or that the asserted concentration or financing dependency is materially wrong. Mixed requires affirmative evidence for both supported and contradicted components.
